title: Server: Parakeet Ultra first, Whisper only when needed (shipped)
lede: Small CPU recognisers that could run beside Whisper base.en in the game's Next.js server, on this VPS's CPU (8-core EPYC, 3 threads, one command at a time). None beats Whisper on its own. As a fast first pass, with Whisper asked only when the game cannot understand the guesses, Parakeet Ultra int8 with the callsigns on frequency as hotwords lifts the Indian-accent proxy from 78.8% to 85.6% exact (p=0.001), ties on US/UK, and answers most commands in about 0.4 s. It now runs in the game.

headline.label: exact command on the Indian-accent proxy: Parakeet, then Whisper (Whisper alone 78.8%, McNemar p=0.001)
exact command on US/UK: Parakeet, then Whisper (Whisper alone 76.9%; not significant)
Parakeet's answer (Whisper ~1.3 s); Whisper is asked for about 1 command in 4

best: Cascade: Parakeet Ultra int8 (sherpa-onnx, callsign hotwords), then Whisper base.en only when not understood. Ultra was right on 11 Indian-proxy clips where Whisper was wrong, and never the other way round. It runs in Node in-process through sherpa-onnx-node, with output identical to Python on 40 of 40 clips.

Granite TurboCTC as the first pass is as good (80.0% / 84.4%) but needs an ONNX port and a front end in JS. Phonon-2.5-English is the fastest good model (0.15 s) but runs only from Python, so it needs a sidecar service.
On US/UK the cascade raises commands sent wrong without a check from 6.3% to 7.5%; on the Indian proxy it lowers them from 7.5% to 3.7%.
shipped: src/app/api/voice/stt: a parakeet engine (sherpa-onnx-node 2.0.1, in the Next.js process, loaded on first use, the same 2-3 threads and the same guards as Whisper: one inference at a time, queue, timeout, per-IP rate limit). ?engine=parakeet|whisper or X-STT-Engine picks one. Without either, the server's first pass is Parakeet; OPENATC_STT_FIRST=whisper restores Whisper alone. Hotwords are the telephony words of the callsigns on frequency, per request. The model files are copied once to ~/.cache/openatc-stt/parakeet-ultra-int8 (ml/stt/RESULTS2.md); without them, Whisper answers.

src/lib/voice/asr-server.ts cascadeStt: the Server recogniser and the Browser engine's second opinion ask the first pass. When the game cannot understand its guesses, the same audio goes to Whisper and both lists are read together (the benchmark's rule). Settings now says "Server (Parakeet + Whisper, tuned for ATC)". The voice demo page uses the same cascade.

Checked in the standalone build (next build, then .next/standalone copied to an empty directory and run on a spare port). Parakeet's transcripts match the benchmark on 40 of 40 clips. On 40 US/UK clips over HTTP the cascade answered in 0.88 s p50 / 2.5 s p95, against 1.32 s / 3.4 s for Whisper alone (Indian proxy: 0.63 s / 2.8 s against 1.36 s / 1.9 s). That pass read the guesses with the rules only, so Whisper was asked more often than in the game. With both models loaded the server uses 2.1-2.3 GB RSS (Whisper alone ~1.2 GB).
Licence: Parakeet Ultra weights CC-BY-4.0 (Moondream's post-training of NVIDIA parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3; ONNX export by the k2-fsa sherpa-onnx project); sherpa-onnx and sherpa-onnx-node Apache-2.0.
failed: No real recordings from the owner yet (ml/data/gold/live/ was empty). Every number is synthetic speech (Kokoro), and the Indian set is a proxy (Kokoro's Hindi voices reading English).

Phonon-2.5-English needs a Python sidecar (a new service: not done). Granite needs an ONNX port (not tried). Parakeet Redux through moondream Photon uses proprietary kernels and reports telemetry; the open sherpa-onnx build of the same weights scores better.
Canary-180M-Flash loops in its decoder (46 s p95).
notes: Cascade rows: the first engine's guesses go through the game chain; only when nothing is understood is Whisper (2-best, prompt) run and both lists mixed. Their latency is an estimate from the quiet pass: first-pass time, plus Whisper's time for the share that asks for it.
Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe 30B (on an L4 GPU) and Google Web Speech are references, not server candidates.
